newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan forces capture rebel-held northern town.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan forces capture rebel-held northern town.

text.p: Sri Lankan security forces have captured a northern town held by Tamil Tiger rebels after fierce air and artillery attacks, military officials said on Sunday.

The town of Nedunkeni has been the scene of fierce fighting for three days on the eastern flank of a three-pronged army push into territory held by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels in the northern Wanni region.
"We have captured Nedunkeni," military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters. Further details of the offensive would be given later, he added.

Two army divisions are on the move on separate axes trying to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, with Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north, military officials said.

The Defence Ministry has only said the main aim of the drive is to capture areas in the shrub-covered Wanni from the LTTE, who are waging a war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
Troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air cover, on Saturday secured the town of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya, after beating off an overnight counter-attack by the rebels.
They are now pushing further north, heading towards the heavily fortified rebel-held town of Puliyankulam.
Military officials said 40 soldiers and more than 128 rebels had been killed in the fighting by Saturday. The latest campaign against the rebels began on Tuesday.
Hospital officials said more than 320 soldiers wounded in the fighting had been sent to hospitals in northern Anuradhapura, Jaffna and Colombo.
Journalists have not yet been allowed into the battle zone.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
